Rashi on Shabbat 96b:10:1.hebrew: גבי הדדי - בתוך אמה אחת, ואין צריכין לזרוק אלא להושיט:
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:10:1.english: Next to each other - Within one cubit, and they do not need to throw [them], but rather to hand [them] over.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:10:2.hebrew: מטו אהדדי במחטין - כשמותחין את החוט, מכין זה את זה במחט:
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:10:2.english: They would reach each other with needles - When they stretch out the thread, they strike one another with the needle.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:11:1.hebrew: בוכיאר - כלי שקנה של ערב נתון בו, שזורקין בין שני דופני היריעה:
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:11:1.english: Shuttle - An implement in which a bobbin of woof [thread] is placed, which they throw between the two sides of the curtain.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:11:2.hebrew: והלא אגדו בידו - חוט של ערב הוא אוחז, והקנה נכרך בחוט ואינו נשמט ממנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:11:2.english: And does he not hold it in his hand - He holds the woof thread, and the reed [shuttle] is wrapped with the thread and does not slip away from him.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:11:3.hebrew: בניסכא בתרא - בחוט האחרון של קנה, שהקנה נשמט מהחוט והבוכיאר נופל:
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:11:3.english: On the final throw - With the last thread of the spool, for the spool slips off the thread and the shuttle falls.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:11:4.hebrew: ניסכא - זריקה אחרונה של חוט, לשון המיסך:
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:11:4.english: Niska - The final throw of the thread, [from] the expression *hameisech* [casting].

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:12:1.hebrew: והא במקום פטור אזלא - בין דופני היריעה, ואין זה רשות הרבים אלא מקום פטור, דאין רחב ד':
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:12:1.english: But doesn't it go in an exempt domain - Between the sides of the tapestry, and this is not a public domain, rather an exempt domain, for it is not four [handbreadths] wide.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:12:2.hebrew: לשואליהן - אורגי יריעה אחרת, ויש לו לזה שנים:
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:12:2.english: To those who borrow from them - Weavers of another tapestry, and this one has two [shuttles].

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:12:3.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: ודילמא שואליהן גביהן הוו יתבין:
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:12:3.english: This is the reading: "And perhaps those who borrow from them were sitting next to them?"

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:12:4.hebrew: מטו אהדדי בחפת - אי גבייהו הוו יתבי, מגיעין ידו של זה בשל זה בשפת היריעה כשמותחין חוט הערב:
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:12:4.english: They would reach one another at the edge - If they were sitting near each other, one's hand would reach the other's at the edge of the curtain when they stretch the woof thread.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:12:5.hebrew: בחפת - כמו חפת חלוקו (יומא ד' עז:):
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:12:5.english: At the hem - Like "the hem of his tunic" (Yoma 77b).

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:13:1.hebrew: שלחופי הוו משלחפי - לעולם גבי הדדי הוו יתבי, אלא שאין מכוונים, אלא זה נמשך לפנים וזה לאחור:
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:13:1.english: They were staggered - In fact, they were sitting next to each other, except that they were not aligned; rather, this one was drawn forward and that one backward.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:13:2.english: And he does not perform [work] from his fellow’s work - For they were all equipped with the tools of their craft and did not need to borrow.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:14:1.hebrew: מעביר ד' אמות הוה - לא תלשן ולא עימרן, אלא העבירן ד' אמות; לכך נהרג:
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:14:1.english: [The wood gatherer] was one who carried four cubits - He did not pluck [the sticks] and did not gather them [into a pile], rather he carried them four cubits; therefore he was executed.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:15:1.hebrew: מעמר - תלושין ומפוזרין היו ועמרן, כדאמרן (לעיל שבת ד' עג:): האי מאן דכניף מלחא חייב משום מעמר:
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:15:1.english: One who gathers - [The sticks] were detached and scattered, and he gathered them, as we said (above, Shabbat 73b): "One who gathers salt is liable on account of gathering."

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:16:1.english: A hidden scroll - That they hid it because one does not write [down] halakhot.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:16:2.hebrew: ואינו חייב אלא אחת - על כרחיך לענין שוגג קאמר ולחטאת, דבמזיד תרי קטלי לא מקטלי, ולהכי פריך: והא אנן תנן כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:16:2.english: And he is liable [for] only one - Perforce, [he] is speaking with regard to an unwitting [transgression] and [liability] for a sin-offering, for in [a case of] an intentional [transgression], two death penalties are not executed. Therefore, [the Gemara] asks: "But we learned [in a Mishnah]," etc.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:17:1.hebrew: ואינו חייב על אחת מהן - מיתה. יש בהן אחת שאינו נהרג עליה, ולא פירש איזו היא. והשתא, לרב יהודה אין זו העברה, שהרי נהרג מקושש עליה; ולמתניתא, אין תולש באותו ספק:
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:17:1.english: And one is not liable for one of them - [For] the death [penalty]. There is one among them for which one is not executed, and [the scroll] did not specify which one it is. Now, according to Rav Yehuda, this [one] is not carrying, for the wood-gatherer was executed for it; and according to the baraita, detaching is not [included] in that doubt.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:1:1.hebrew: מכדי זריקה תולדה דהוצאה - על כרחיך תולדה היא, דלא נמנית באבות מלאכות; ותולדה דהוצאה היא, שאין לך לתתה תולדת אב אחר, דמעין הוצאה היא האמורה באבות מלאכות:
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:1:1.english: After all, throwing is a subcategory of carrying out - Perforce it is a subcategory, since it was not counted among the primary categories of labor; and it is a subcategory of carrying out, for you cannot assign it [as] a subcategory of another primary category, as it is akin to carrying out, which is stated among the primary categories of labor.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:1:2.hebrew: מחנה לויה ר"ה היא - שהיו הכל מצויין אצל משה רבינו:
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:1:2.english: The camp of the Levites was a public domain - For everyone was frequently present with Moses our teacher.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:1:3.english: From your private domain - From your tents.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:2:1.english: That his work was completed - That the donation was sufficient to complete [the work].

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:4:1.hebrew: סברא היא - להיות הכנסה תולדת הוצאה, שהיא מעין לה, כשאר תולדות שהיא מעין מלאכות:
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:4:1.english: It is a logical inference - For carrying in to be a subcategory of carrying out, as it is similar to it, like [all] other subcategories, which are similar to [the primary] labors.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:5:1.english: Since one is liable for this and one is liable for that - As we learned in the Mishnah (above, Chapter 1, 2a): "[If] the poor man stretched his hand inside."

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:6:1.english: The practical ramification - of all primary categories of labor.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:6:2.hebrew: שתי אבות - דלא דמיין, ושתי תולדות דשתי אבות:
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:6:2.english: Two primary categories - That do not resemble [one another], and two subcategories [means] of two primary categories.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:7:1.hebrew: ולר"א כו' - במסכת כריתות בפרק אמרו לו:
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:7:1.english: And according to Rabbi Eliezer, etc. - In Tractate Keritot, in the chapter [entitled] Amru Lo.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:8:1.english: And that which we learned [in a Mishnah] - In our chapter.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:8:2.english: On a wall - As [the Gemara] establishes it [as referring] to a fat pressed fig that sticks [to the wall].

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:8:3.hebrew: כזורק באויר - ופטור, דלא נח ברשות הרבים, דאין רה"ר למעלה מעשרה; וברה"י נמי לא נח, שאינו מקום מסוים שיהא רחבו ד', שהרי לא נח בראש הכותל, אלא בפניו:
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:8:3.english: As if he threw it into the air - And he is exempt, because it did not come to rest in the public domain, since there is no public domain above ten [handbreadths]; nor did it come to rest in a private domain, as it is not a distinct place whose width is four [handbreadths], for it did not come to rest on the top of the wall, but rather on its face.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:8:4.hebrew: כזורק בארץ - דאויר רה"ר הוא וחייב. וכיון דאויר רה"ר הוא ונח בכל דהו, מיחייב; ורשותא לנפשיה לא הוי, לא כרמלית ולא מקום פטור, הואיל ובפניו נח, ולא נח בראשו שיהא מקום מסוים:
Rashi on Shabbat 96b:8:4.english: As if he threw [it] onto the ground - For it is the airspace of the public domain, and he is liable. And since it is the airspace of the public domain and it came to rest on any minimal [spot], he is liable; and it is not a domain unto itself — neither a karmelit nor an exempt area — since it came to rest on its [vertical] face, and did not come to rest on its top, such that it would be a distinct place.

Rashi on Shabbat 96b:9:1.english: Those who sewed [the] tapestries - [This refers to] embroidery work.

Tosafot on Shabbat 96b:13:1.hebrew: ודילמא שלחופי הוו משלחפי - הכי נמי הוה מצי למיפרך: דילמא תוך ארבע אמות הוו יתבי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 96b:13:1.english: And perhaps they were staggered - [The Gemara] could also have asked: Perhaps they were sitting within four cubits [of one another].

Tosafot on Shabbat 96b:1:1.hebrew: הוצאה גופה היכא כתיבא - ואע"ג שהיתה במשכן, כדאמר "הם הורידו קרשים מעגלה כו'", מכל מקום אי לאו דכתיב לא הוה מחייבי עלה, לפי שמלאכה גרועה היא, כדפי' לעיל (שבת דף ב.):
Tosafot on Shabbat 96b:1:1.english: Where is carrying out itself written - And even though it existed in the Tabernacle, as [the Gemara] says, "they lowered the boards from the wagon, etc.," nevertheless, if it were not written [in Scripture], they would not be liable for it, because it is an inferior labor, as I explained above (Shabbat 2a).

Tosafot on Shabbat 96b:2:1.hebrew: וממאי דבשבת קאי - ר"ח ל"ג כל זה עד "אשכחן הוצאה", דהא אפילו בחול קאי נפקא ליה שפיר דהוצאה מלאכה הוא, דהא רחמנא קרייה מלאכה, כדכתיב: "ואיש ואשה אל יעשו עוד מלאכה לתרומת הקדש", וכתיב: "ויכלא העם מהביא"; אלמא קרי להוצאה מלאכה, וכן דריש בהדיא בירושלמי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 96b:2:1.english: And from where [do we know] that he was standing on Shabbat - Rabbeinu Chananel does not have in his text all of this until "We have found carrying out [is a labor]," for even if he was standing on a weekday, it is well derived that carrying out is a labor, since the Merciful One calls it "labor," as it is written: "Let neither man nor woman do any more labor for the offering of the Sanctuary," and it is written: "And the people were restrained from bringing"; thus [Scripture] calls carrying out "labor," and so it expounds explicitly in the Jerusalem Talmud.

Tosafot on Shabbat 96b:4:1.hebrew: הכנסה מנלן סברא הוא כו' - וא"ת: מה צריך להאי סברא, כיון דהוות במשכן, כדאמר: "הם העלו קרשים לעגלה" כו', דהא בסמוך משמע גבי זריקה דאם היתה במשכן הוה אתי ליה שפיר? וי"ל: דבזריקה נמי איכא סברא — מה לי ע"י הוצאה, מה לי ע"י זריקה — דאי לאו סברא לא הוה מחשבינן לה תולדה דהוצאה; ואי לא הוות נמי במשכן, לא הוה מחייבינן עלה מסברא, לפי שמלאכה גרועה היא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 96b:4:1.english: "From where do we [derive] carrying in? It is a logical inference, etc." - And if you ask: Why is this logical inference needed, since [carrying in] was [performed] in the Tabernacle, as [the Gemara] says, "They lifted the boards onto the wagon," etc. — for immediately below, regarding throwing, it is implied that if it had been [performed] in the Tabernacle, it would be derived well [from there]? And one can answer: Regarding throwing as well, there is a logical inference — what difference is there to me [whether it is] through carrying out, [and] what difference is there to me [whether it is] through throwing? — for if not for the logical inference, we would not consider it a subcategory of carrying out. And if it had not been [performed] in the Tabernacle either, we would not hold [one] liable for it based on logical inference [alone], because it is an inferior labor.

Tosafot on Shabbat 96b:7:1.hebrew: ולרבי אליעזר דמחייב אתולדה במקום אב אמאי קרי לה אב כו' - הוה מצי למימר דנפקא מינה לענין התראה, כדפי' בפ' כלל גדול (לע. ל עג:), ואיכא למימר דהיינו דקמשני: "הך דהוות במשכן חשיבא כו'". אית דגרסי: "הך דהוות במשכן חשיבא — קרי לה אב, והך דלא הוות במשכן חשיבא — קרי לה תולדה"; ולפי זה יש מלאכות דהוו במשכן, כגון מנכש ומשקה זרעים, דלא חשיבי ולא הוו אבות. וכן אי גרסינן: "דהוות במשכן וחשיבא — קרי לה אב". אבל אי גרסי': "הך דהוות במשכן — חשיבא וקרי לה אב, הך דלא הוות במשכן — לא חשיבא וקרי לה תולדה", לפי זה התולדות לא היו במשכן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 96b:7:1.english: And according to Rabbi Eliezer, who renders one liable for a subcategory together with a primary category, why is it called a primary category, etc. - [The Gemara] could have said that there is a practical difference with respect to forewarning, as explained in Perek Kelal Gadol (73b), and one can say that this is what it answers: "That which was significant in the Tabernacle, etc." There are those who read [the text]: "That which was significant in the Tabernacle — one calls it a primary category, and that which was not significant in the Tabernacle — one calls it a subcategory"; and according to this, there are labors that were in the Tabernacle, such as weeding and watering seeds, that are not significant and are not primary categories. And similarly, if we read: "that which was in the Tabernacle and was significant — one calls it a primary category." However, if we read: "That which was in the Tabernacle — is significant and one calls it a primary category; that which was not in the Tabernacle — is not significant and one calls it a subcategory," according to this, the subcategories were not in the Tabernacle.

Tosafot on Shabbat 96b:7:2.english: Alternatively, that which is written is called a primary category - This formulation is only needed because of [the labor of] carrying out:
